clue.text: Sailor in charge of vessel showing skill

parts.note: a hand is a member of a ship's crew, a deckhand
a raft is a simple floating craft

explanation.surface: A naval officer commanding a ship demonstrates his expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' tempts you towards CRAFT, but the C has already come from 'in charge'; the vessel is only a RAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Handicraft is manual skill in making things, so the word can stand for a practical skill or art.

clue.text: Game with white wine — very irregular

parts.note: hock is a British name for white wine from the German Rhineland

indicators.note: irregular here means taking the letters of the word very at intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Someone drinking white wine at a match behaves very erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' asks for alternate letters of 'very', here the second and fourth, E and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Hockey is a team sport played with sticks and a ball or puck.

indicators.note: for signals that one letter stands in the place of another within the word

parts.note: almost means very nearly
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
B is the cricket scoring abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket question: was a batsman nearly out just short of his half-century?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled for fifty' means put B in place of L: NEARLY becomes NEARBY. Cricket is the British bat-and-ball game; fifty runs is a half-century.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand is a short distance away, in the vicinity.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Notices inert form at crossroads (12)' for INTERVENTION: an anagram of INERT gives INTER, but no reading of 'Notices' or 'crossroads' supplies VENTION and NOTICES INERT has a C the answer lacks; no blog found.

clue.text: Casanova finds love in French street

indicators.note: in means the letter for love is placed inside the French word for street

parts.note: rue is the French word for street
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A notorious seducer discovers romance in a Parisian road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' looks like part of the romantic picture but is the tennis score zero, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova was a famous womaniser, and a roué is a debauched pleasure-seeking man.

clue.text: Rook's after front place on board

indicators.note: after means the chess-piece word follows the word for front

parts.note: fore means front, as in the forepart of a ship
the rook in chess is also called a castle; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A chess remark: the rook moves behind a forward square on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface makes 'board' a chessboard, but it means on board ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle is the forward part of a ship below or at the deck, a location aboard a vessel.

indicators.note: round means the word for gross encloses the abbreviation for about

parts.note: the gross is the whole sum before deductions
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A movie is disgusting, give or take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' and 'gross' suggest a bad movie, but the film is a thin layer, and gross is a total.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a layer of dirt or froth floating on a liquid, a thin surface film.

parts.note: two readings: a well-known British dictionary would define the word, and the atria are themselves the upper cavities of the heart

explanation.walkthrough: Atria are the two upper cavities of the heart, and the British dictionary of the same name is where you would look the word up.
explanation.definitionFit: The atria are heart compartments, and the Chambers Dictionary is a standard reference book for word meanings.

clue.text: Young lady embracing heavy metal fools

indicators.note: embracing means the word for a young lady wraps round the metal

parts.note: miss is a title or word for a young unmarried woman
lead is a notably dense metal, chemical symbol Pb

explanation.surface: A girl into loud rock music makes fools of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' suggests the music genre, but it is simply the dense metal LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead people is to deceive them, so as a verb it means fools or tricks.

parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea, so this is the body that provides a rescue service at sea, not a utility company

explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like a water or gas main from a utility company, but the main is the high sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastguard is the organisation that watches the coast and rescues people in trouble at sea.

clue.text: Swells born with silver spoon, initially

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word spoon

explanation.surface: Upper-class toffs come into the world with every advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swells' reads as posh people, which fits the silver spoon, but it is a verb meaning bulges.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth bags when it bulges or sags outward, so the verb means swells.

parts.note: a mandarin is a senior bureaucrat, originally a Chinese imperial official
a duck is a score of nought by a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A bird's-eye view: a civil servant posts a dismal cricket score.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the British bat-and-ball game, a batsman out without scoring makes a DUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandarin duck is a brightly coloured East Asian waterfowl species.

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
M is the abbreviation of monsieur, the French for mister
to bay is to bark or howl like a hound

explanation.surface: A French sailor heads off east from a coastal inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like a coastal inlet, fitting the sailing picture, but it is a dog's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go on board a ship and begin a voyage.

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the Latin word is removed

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus, printed after a quoted error
a rabble is a disorderly crowd, a mob; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether a cruel crowd is sporting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle I out of SIC, leaving SC.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is a word-building board game played with lettered tiles.

parts.note: reads like a horse ridden out on a shoot, but describes a toy steed on a stick that also names a pet topic someone keeps riding, often a gripe

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a grouse shoot on horseback; instead, the toy horse doubles as a favourite grievance one keeps returning to.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobbyhorse is a child's stick horse and, figuratively, a pet subject or complaint someone keeps raising.

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are moved about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre censor went over a terrible drama and cut it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like the drama being censored, but it signals rearranging CENSORED DIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reconsidered something is to have thought it over again, reassessed it.

clue.text: Gets account with lots of paper

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Someone opens a bank account and is handed piles of stationery.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to obtain or come to possess it.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A comic tale that a single performer acts out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acted out' reads as a performance, but 'out' signals rearranging ONE ACTED.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing tale about a real incident.

indicators.note: changing indicates the letters of the three words are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The police reform a violent prisoner, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' suggests violence, but it is a police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A constabulary is a police force for a given district.

clue.text: Drink with east enders woman ? B… Great!

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
in a Cockney East End London accent the H is dropped, so her becomes 'er
the letter as printed

explanation.surface: A Cockney drinks with a woman whose name starts with B, and it is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, from London's East End, traditionally drop their H's, so HER becomes 'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb, as an exclamation, expresses that something is excellent or splendid.

definitions.meaning: a long wooden seat with a high back and arms
to sort out or resolve a dispute or disorder

explanation.definitionFit: A settle is a high-backed wooden seat, and to settle a matter is to resolve it.

clue.text: Expose united nations finding dummy explosive

parts.note: a clot, like a dummy, is a stupid person
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A whistleblower reveals that the UN has found a fake bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dummy explosive' reads as a fake bomb; in fact 'dummy' is a fool and 'explosive' is HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclothe someone is to strip them, leaving the body bare and uncovered.

indicators.note: shower suggests the word under is scattered like drops of rain into a new order

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A romantic couple shelter together beneath a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' as rain is the anagram signal on UNDER, giving ENDUR; 'sweetheart' is the central letter of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate or bear it.

clue.text: Join up to become an orchestra member

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for join is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to abut is to adjoin or touch along a border

explanation.surface: An invitation to enlist in an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join up' sounds like enlisting; 'up' reverses ABUT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the largest brass instrument in a symphony orchestra.

indicators.note: we hear means the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: rude means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: Someone is angry and coarse, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' wants to be angry, alongside 'vulgar', but it is the noun for a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen.

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A crafty naked model is up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' reads as the artist's sitter, but it is a verb signalling rearranging ARTFUL NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraudulent means obtained or done by deception, so cheating or crooked.

clue.text: …the woman had shortly to peel off

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
had is shortened to 'd in a contraction, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A woman had to strip off her clothes quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' reads as 'soon', but it shortens HAD to its contraction 'D.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed skin or leaves is to cast it off, to lose an outer layer.

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in a letter heading
a mark is a score in a test
able means capable or clever

explanation.surface: A bright student's exam result is impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remarkable is worthy of attention, striking or extraordinary.
